title: All-Cheese Connoisseur Board
seo_title: Cheese Board With No Meat for 8–12: Six-Cheese Flight & Plan
description: An all-cheese connoisseur board for 8–12: Brillat-Savarin, chèvre, Taleggio, Fontina, aged Manchego and Parmigiano, tasted mild to strong, with honeycomb and quince.
hook: Six cheeses, one flight, no meat to hide behind: a board for real cheese lovers, tasted from mild to strong.
why: Six cheeses arranged as a flight, two soft, two semi-soft and two hard, so guests taste their way from mild and creamy to sharp and crystalline. The order does a lot of the work: the same cheeses taste better in sequence than scattered.

Each cheese gets a partner: honeycomb for the triple-crème, quince paste for the Manchego and aged balsamic for the Parmigiano. Crackers go from plain at the mild end to walnut raisin crisps at the bold end.

timeline.what: Take the Parmigiano and Manchego out of the fridge.
Take out the Fontina and Taleggio.
Take out the triple-crème and chèvre; slice the baguette.
Place the cheeses in tasting order, mild to strong.
Add the honeycomb, quince, fruit and crackers.

faq.q: How many cheeses should be on a cheese board?
faq.a: Three to five is typical. Six works for a dedicated cheese lovers' board, at about 1 oz of each per guest.

faq.q: What order do you eat cheeses in?
faq.a: Mild to strong: fresh and soft first, then semi-soft and washed-rind, then hard aged cheeses.

faq.q: What wine goes with a cheese flight?
faq.a: Champagne goes with almost every cheese. Otherwise a dry white for the soft cheeses and a light red for the hard ones.
